newsitem.title: USA: Miami carnival returns year after Cuba shoot-down.
newsitem.headline: Miami carnival returns year after Cuba shoot-down.

text.p: More than a million people were expected to join the party at Miami's huge carnival, which returns after being cancelled last year after Cuba shot down two planes flown by Miami-based exiles.
"We're back," Tony Goitia, president of the local Kiwanis Club, which organises the Feb. 18 to March 9 carnival, said at a launch party Wednesday night.

Amid the singing and dancing at what organisers called the largest Hispanic festival in the United States, they said they hoped to break the world record for the most people dancing the Macarena. The record of 50,000 was set by dancers at New York's Yankee Stadium in 1995.
The carnival is already in the Guinness Book of Records for the world's largest conga line. More than 119,000 carnival-goers danced to the music of Gloria Estefan in 1988.

The climax will be a 23-block street party March 9 in Little Havana, centred on Calle Ocho (8th Street), the heartland of the Cuban-American community. "Calle Ocho is the big one. Calle Ocho is our event," Goitia said.

Last year's carnival was cancelled as the Cuban American community mourned the deaths of four exiles belonging to the Brothers to the Rescue organisation, who were shot down by Cuban jets on Feb. 24 over the Florida Straits.
